request.spec:
People have a position in the list. Up and down buttons on the row swap the person with the one
above or below (PERSON_MOVED name=<name> position=<new position, counting from 1>); the top row
cannot move up nor the bottom row down (refused with an error on the row). The list, the rollup lines
and every action that works in list order follow the positions. New people go to the end.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
People have a position in the list. Up and down buttons on the row swap the person with the one
above or below (PERSON_MOVED name=<name> position=<new position, counting from 1>); the top row
cannot move up nor the bottom row down (refused with an error on the row). The list, the rollup lines
and every action that works in list order follow the positions. New people go to the end.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People now have a place in the list, and each row has Up and Down buttons to move them. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**Stored data**
- A new migration, `V61__person_position.sql`, adds a `position` column to people. People already on a sheet keep the order they were added in.
- The people list is now sorted by position (ties broken by id).
- Everything that works in list order reads that same list, so it all follows the new positions without further changes: the list on screen, the rollup lines, bulk open, settle and reassign, bulk grade, and the snapshot written when the sheet's today changes.
- New people go to the end. People transferred in from another sheet also go to the end.
- The view of the sheet as of a past date also follows the positions.

**Server**
- A new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/move`, takes `{direction: up|down, by}`.
- It swaps the person with their neighbour and writes `PERSON_MOVED sheet=… by=… name=… position=<new position, counting from 1>` to the audit file.
- Moving the top person up or the bottom one down is refused with a 400, and nothing is written to the store or the audit file.
- The new Java classes are in the `person` package: `ValidateMove`, `MovePerson`, `RecordPersonMoved`, `MoveRequest` and `PersonMove`.

**Front end**
- `features/move/move.slot.tsx` adds the `person-move-up` and `person-move-down` buttons to each row.
- A refused move shows the row's `person-error`, which clears on the next action taken on that row. A successful move reloads the people list.

I also changed the code comments and endpoint descriptions that said people are listed "in the order they were added" to say "list order".

Two edge cases the test doesn't cover:
- **Hidden retired people:** a move swaps with the neighbour in the full list. When retired people are hidden, a move next to one swaps with them, so nothing appears to change on screen.
- **People added at the same moment:** if two people are added at exactly the same time they can end up with the same position. The id decides their order, and a move between them still works.
